title: Augmented comparison of Cartan--Eilenberg bicomplexes
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and F:A→B an exact additive functor. Let K and L be Z-indexed cochain complexes, u:F(K)→L a chain map, and I,J bicomplexes with complex index Z and resolution index N [def-sp-double-complex-total], augmented from K[0] and L[0] in the resolution degree. Assume I and J vanish below respective common bounds in the complex degree. Assume their augmented object, cycle, boundary and homology columns are quasi-isomorphisms from the corresponding objects concentrated in resolution degree zero. Assume the object, cycle, boundary and homology terms of J are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No injectivity assumption on I is imposed. Then there is a bicomplex morphism φ:F(I)→J satisfying, for every p, F(εIᵖ) followed by φᵖ,⁰ equals uᵖ followed by εJᵖ, with the degree-zero single objects identified by singleObjXSelf. No total-complex or filtration conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: For every degree $q$, decompose the bounded-below complex into the exact sequences $0\to Z^q\to K^q\to B^{q+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^q\to Z^q\to H^q(K)\to0$, and make the same decompositions for $L$. Exactness of $F$ carries these sequences and the exact augmented rows of $I_K$ to exact sequences and exact augmented rows of $F(I_K)$. The six Cartan--Eilenberg conditions stated in the item give the required injective-resolution rows for $J_L$, and for its $Z$, $B$, and $H_{II}$ pieces. Source injectivity is not needed: augmented exact source columns suffice.

We construct the row maps by induction on $q$, along the sequence $0\to B^q\to Z^q\to H^q\to0$, $0\to Z^q\to K^q\to B^{q+1}\to0$ of Step 1. The induction claim at $q$ is that a map $\varphi_B^q$ from the row $F(\operatorname{Im}(d_{II}:I_K^{\bullet,q-1}\to I_K^{\bullet,q}))$ to the corresponding row of $J_L$ has been constructed, compatible with the augmentations (through $u$). Below the lowest nonzero degree all rows are zero, and in the lowest degree $B^q=0$, so $\varphi_B^q=0$ starts the induction. Given $\varphi_B^q$: (a) the $H^q$ row map $\varphi_H^q$ is obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso], applied to the augmentation $F(H^q(K))[0]\to F(H^q_{II}(I_K))$, which is a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism because $0\to F(H^q(K))\to F(H^q_{II}(I_K)^{0})\to F(H^q_{II}(I_K)^{1})\to\cdots$ is exact, and to the map $F(H^q(K))\to H^q(L)\to H^q_{II}(J_L)^{0}$ into the bounded-below injective complex $H^q_{II}(J_L)$; (b) the $Z^q$ row map $\varphi_Z^q$ is the middle map $\varphi_B$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] for the short exact sequence of exact augmented complexes $0\to F(B^q\text{-row})\to F(Z^q\text{-row})\to F(H^q\text{-row})\to0$ over $0\to F(B^q)\to F(Z^q)\to F(H^q(K))\to0$, the target horseshoe $0\to B^q\text{-row}\to Z^q\text{-row}\to H^q_{II}\text{-row}$ of $J_L$ (injective resolutions by (4)--(6), degreewise exact, zero for $p<0$ by (2)) and the endpoint maps $\varphi_B^q,\varphi_H^q$; (c) the $B^{q+1}$ row map $\varphi_B^{q+1}$ is obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] exactly as in (a), for the row $F(\operatorname{Im}(d_{II}:I_K^{\bullet,q}\to I_K^{\bullet,q+1}))$ augmented by $F(B^{q+1})$; (d) the $K^q$ row map $\phi^{\bullet,q}$ is the middle map $\varphi_B$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] for $0\to F(Z^q\text{-row})\to F(I_K^{\bullet,q})\to F(B^{q+1}\text{-row})\to0$ over $0\to F(Z^q)\to F(K^q)\to F(B^{q+1})\to0$, the target horseshoe given by (3)--(5), and the endpoint maps $\varphi_Z^q,\varphi_B^{q+1}$. Each row map is chosen exactly once: $\varphi_B$ and $\varphi_H$ by the quasi-isomorphism lift, $\varphi_Z$ and $\phi^{\bullet,q}$ as horseshoe middle maps, so the three-term compatibilities of (b) and (d) hold for the maps actually used, and $\varphi_B^{q+1}$ continues the induction.

Each chosen original-object column map is a chain map in resolution degree. In complex degree p the source horizontal differential factors through its boundary column in degree p+1 and its cycle column in degree p+1; the target differential has the analogous factorization through the target boundary and cycle columns. The endpoint squares of the original-column horseshoe lift, the cycle-column horseshoe lift, and the retained boundary comparison show that each factor commutes with the chosen maps. Thus the column maps commute with the horizontal differential. They assemble into a bicomplex morphism; their augmentation equations give the displayed degree-zero identity via singleObjXSelf.
